forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: Weekly Sunday-only cadence — no intra-week delta permitted. Held at 0.75. Material for Sunday 2026-06-07 review: (a) dissolution bill first reading passed 106-0 on June 1, accelerating election path; (b) coalition seat count approximately 60 under contested methodology with 61-seat majority threshold in question; (c) polling projects Netanyahu bloc at 49-52 seats, well below governing threshold. F5-CASCADE clause added: if F5 (dissolution second reading) resolves YES, F2 resolves YES simultaneously.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if a party-withdrawal letter is formally submitted to the Knesset Speaker and publicly confirmed by the departing party and acknowledged by the Speaker's office, OR if Netanyahu formally announces an early election date earlier than 2026-10-27, OR if a government-initiated dissolution bill passes all formal Knesset plenum readings by majority vote. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Primary: Knesset official record or Times of Israel/Haaretz confirmed by at least one additional named outlet. Polling alone does not resolve. Reviewed weekly on Sundays only; no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. A party-withdrawal letter formally submitted to the Knesset Speaker constitutes loss of coalition majority without requiring a plenary roll-call vote, provided the withdrawal is publicly confirmed by the party and acknowledged by the Speaker's office. VOLUNTARY DISSOLUTION ADDENDUM: a government-initiated dissolution bill passing all formal Knesset plenum readings by a majority vote counts as YES. F5 CASCADE: if F5 (2026-05-31-knesset-dissolution-bill-second-reading-by-june-15) resolves YES, F2 resolves YES simultaneously.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (containing both a Hormuz/ceasefire element AND an explicit nuclear negotiation framework component) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Analyst proposed p=0.04 — corrected to schema minimum 0.05. Iran's state media (Tasnim) reported June 1 that the Iranian negotiating team formally suspended dialogues and exchange of texts through mediators, citing Israeli attacks in Lebanon as violations of ceasefire preconditions. Confirmed independently by Washington Post, NPR, Washington Times, and Euronews. US struck Iranian radar and command-control sites at Qeshm Island inside the Strait of Hormuz and at Goruk on the mainland over May 31–June 1; Iran's IRGC fired missiles targeting Kuwait-based US forces. Trump publicly contradicted the suspension, asserting talks continued at a 'rapid pace,' but no Iranian-side confirmation of resumed contact was observable by June 2 morning. Iranian MFA has not accepted Trump's May 31 tightened language on uranium retrieval and Hormuz wording. With 72 hours remaining to the June 5 horizon and no named principals positioned to sign, resolution as YES is near-foreclosed. Set at schema floor 0.05. AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO language must be drafted by EOD June 4 per existing Judge flag.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official (Trump personally, or Secretary Rubio citing Trump's explicit written public authority) AND a named Iranian official (President Pezeshkian or his office, OR FM Araghchi with explicit Pezeshkian office endorsement within 72h) both publicly confirm a signed written framework containing both (a) a Hormuz/ceasefire element AND (b) an explicit nuclear negotiation framework component. Verbal 'agreement in principle' without document text or dual authentication does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Iranian state outlets (IRNA, Press TV, Fars) alone do NOT satisfy the Iranian principal confirmation requirement without independent corroboration from a Tier 1 non-state outlet. Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or US State Dept press release also resolves if dual-confirmed.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran FM Araghchi confirms but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. VP Vance confirmation alone, without Trump's explicit public authority delegation, does NOT trigger YES. A ceasefire MOU without nuclear framework component = NOT YES. 'Agreement in principle' phrasing without document text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If horizon passes with no signed document confirmed by both sides: RESOLVED-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a named US principal (Trump personally, or Secretary Rubio on Trump's explicit public authority) AND a named Iranian principal (President Pezeshkian or FM Araghchi confirmed by Pezeshkian's office) publicly confirm a signed written MOU, ceasefire extension framework, or comparable accord before EOD 2026-06-07?
forecasts.delta_reason: Analyst proposed 0.10; DA partial accept raised floor to 0.18. Iran formally suspended negotiations via mediators June 1 (Tasnim, Washington Post, NPR, Washington Times confirmed); US struck Qeshm Island and Goruk; Iran fired missiles at Kuwait-based US forces. DA credits Iran's prior suspension/resumption pattern — January 2025 and September 2025 suspensions both resumed within weeks — suggesting 'suspension' language does not historically foreclose near-term talks. IRGC same-day public attribution of retaliatory strike may reflect escalation management rather than full rupture. Trump's insistence on 'rapid pace' not corroborated by Iranian side but White House officials (per PBS) had a 60-day proposal nearly signed as of May 28. Five days remain to June 7. Analyst's 0.10 is too low given suspension/resumption precedent; DA's 0.20 ceiling is too high given active strikes on Iranian territory. Judge sets p=0.18. 'Comparable accord' clarification added: requires signed written document confirmed by named principals on both sides; verbal announcements and unilateral statements do not qualify.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the White House (Trump personally, or SecState Rubio citing Trump's explicit written public authority) AND Iran's presidency (Pezeshkian or his office, OR FM Araghchi with explicit Pezeshkian office endorsement within 72h) both publicly confirm a signed written MOU, ceasefire extension agreement, or framework accord before EOD 2026-06-07. 'Comparable accord' means a signed written document confirmed by named principals on both sides; verbal announcements, oral agreements, or unilateral statements by one party do not qualify. Text authenticated by both sides or published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept/Iran MFA with dual acknowledgment counts.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At least two of: Reuters, AP, Axios, Bloomberg, or official government statement from US State Dept or Iranian presidency. Iranian state media alone insufficient. Social media posts by Trump alone count only if Iran's side confirms within 24h.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Envoy-level agreement without principal (Trump/Pezeshkian) confirmation within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iran FM Araghchi confirms but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. VP Vance confirmation alone without Trump's explicit public authority = NOT sufficient. forecasts.question: Will the Knesset dissolution bill pass both its first AND second formal plenum readings before EOD 2026-06-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Analyst proposed 0.55; DA range 0.62-0.65; Judge sets 0.62 at DA lower bound. First reading passed 106-0 in Knesset plenum June 1, following 8-0 House Committee vote the same day. Both unanimous — confirms full coalition alignment at the first-reading stage. Judge flag from Day 94 confirmed. DA opposing narrative correctly identifies the election-date dispute (haredi factions preferring September, Netanyahu preferring late October) as a real, unresolved structural obstacle: under Israeli procedure, the second reading requires an election date embedded in bill text, and the coalition must resolve this dispute before second reading proceeds. Times of Israel and Haaretz confirm date dispute is active; JNS confirms no second-reading date set. 106-0 signal is unambiguously strong; Analyst's 0.55 understates it. Upper bound of 0.65+ would require confirmed second-reading date or coalition agreement on election date, neither observed. Judge sets 0.62.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset plenary has conducted and formally recorded a roll-call vote passing both the first AND second readings of the dissolution bill before EOD 2026-06-15. Official Knesset record or confirmed by Times of Israel/Haaretz/Jerusalem Post.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Primary: Knesset official record. Secondary: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Jerusalem Post confirmed by at least one additional named outlet.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A reading counts only if a final roll-call vote is recorded in Knesset official minutes. Adjournment mid-vote, procedural suspension, or committee referral without plenary vote does not satisfy resolution criteria. If first reading passes but second reading delayed past June 15: RESOLVED-NO. If bill amended in committee between readings and no second reading conducted before June 15: RESOLVED-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire (45-day extension announced May 15, 2026, expiring ~June 29) be formally extended again OR replaced by a new framework agreement before EOD 2026-06-29?
forecasts.delta_reason: Analyst proposed 0.48; DA recommended hold at 0.58 pending June 2-3 outcome; Judge sets 0.50. Confirmed adverse movements observable before June 2-3 talks conclude: Netanyahu ordered strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs June 1; IDF forces crossed the Litani River (deepest incursion since 2000); Iran formally suspended US negotiations explicitly citing Lebanese ceasefire violations. Trump announced a partial ceasefire arrangement June 1 (Beirut suburb strikes to halt in exchange for Hezbollah restraint), but Netanyahu stated publicly the military 'will continue to operate as planned,' and Lebanon's state news agency confirmed overnight strikes continued. Washington's proposal describes a permanent de-escalation framework — a harder deliverable than a simple 60-day rollover. June 2-3 talks confirmed as scheduled but without a communique observable by June 2 morning. DA's hold at 0.58 does not credit confirmed adverse ground movements; Analyst's 0.48 pre-empts June 2-3 outcome. Judge sets 0.50 as midpoint. If June 2-3 ends without communique, recommend immediate reduction to ~0.38-0.42 at next update.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire is either formally extended again OR replaced by a new framework agreement confirmed before EOD 2026-06-29. Formal extension requires: (a) a written agreement signed by Israeli and Lebanese delegations, OR (b) an official statement by a named principal (not spokesperson) from BOTH sides confirming the extension or replacement. US State Department official statement, Israeli PM office, or Lebanese Presidency confirmation required.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Primary: Reuters or AP with named principals from both the Israeli and Lebanese sides. US State Department spokesperson statement alone is insufficient and must be corroborated by at least one named principal from the Israeli or Lebanese government. Hezbollah unilateral declarations alone do not resolve YES.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral extension announced by one party only = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. De facto ceasefire without formal announcement by named principals from both sides by EOD June 29 = NO. A US-brokered roadmap announcement without Israeli and Lebanese principal confirmation does not qualify. Continued IDF strikes in south Lebanon at porous-truce intensity do NOT constitute ceasefire collapse or non-renewal for resolution purposes.
